title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Shreveport, LA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Shreveport refinery, Haynesville pipeline, data center and base construction welding inspectors: Part C, Part B and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Shreveport and Bossier City: Six Days for Refinery, Pipeline, Data Center and Military Construction Welding Inspectors
html:
Northwest Louisiana's welding work is spread across four very different kinds of job. Gas gathered from the Haynesville Shale moves south through new pipelines. A refinery in Shreveport runs process units, tanks and piping that need repair welding at every turnaround. Data center campuses and military construction at Barksdale Air Force Base are bringing structural steel and mechanical piping to both sides of the Red River. And a mill at the Port of Caddo-Bossier makes seamless steel pipe for oilfield and pipeline customers. An inspector who can read the governing code and apply it fairly is useful in all four.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day preparation course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination for welders, pipefitters, pipeline helpers moving into inspection, QC staff, NDT technicians and field engineers in Shreveport, Bossier City and the wider Ark-La-Tex. AWS, the American Welding Society, administers the examination and grants the certification; you apply to AWS on your own behalf and must personally meet its education, experience and vision requirements. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no access to the examination or to candidates' results. There is no Atlantis classroom in Shreveport. You can take the six days online at your own pace, have them delivered for a crew at your employer's yard or site, or book them one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. What each of the six days covers is explained on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Haynesville gas and the pipelines to the Gulf: API 1104 country

In February 2026 the US Energy Information Administration reported that two pipelines built to carry Haynesville production, the Louisiana Energy Gateway at 1.8 billion cubic feet per day and the New Generation Gas Gathering system at 1.7 billion cubic feet per day, were both in service by October 2025, connecting the Haynesville formation to the Gillis Hub in southeastern Louisiana. Projects like those, and the gathering lines, compressor stations and treating plants that feed them, are typical places for Shreveport welders to work alongside a welding inspector.

Pipeline girth welds in the United States are generally qualified and accepted against API 1104, and API 1104 in its 22nd edition is one of the AWS Part C options. A CWI on a spread checks that welders are qualified for the procedure, that bevels, fit-up, preheat and interpass control follow it, that visual acceptance is applied consistently and that repairs and cut-outs are recorded. Compressor and treating stations add facility piping, which is commonly built to ASME B31.3 or B31.8 depending on the owner's specification, so station inspectors sometimes weigh the ASME package against API 1104 before they choose. Reading: API 1104 explained.

On a mainline spread the welding inspector's day follows the crews down the right-of-way. Bevels and line-up come first, then a check that every welder on the joint holds a qualification for the procedure in use, then preheat, the time between root and hot pass, and the condition of each completed weld before coating. The inspector marks rejected welds, tracks repairs and cut-outs, coordinates with the NDT crew whose results are judged against the same standard, and writes a daily report the owner's representative will read closely. Little of that is glamorous, but a spread that runs on accurate records is one that finishes without arguments.

The Shreveport refinery and the ASME option

EIA's refinery capacity report as of January 1, 2026 lists Calumet Shreveport Refining LLC in Shreveport with 57,000 barrels per calendar day of operating atmospheric crude distillation capacity, along with vacuum distillation and other downstream units. A refinery of that kind keeps welders and inspectors busy in two modes: steady maintenance repairs, and turnarounds when units come down and a large contract workforce replaces piping, nozzles, exchanger components and tank parts in a compressed window.

Repair and alteration welding on refinery piping and pressure equipment is usually controlled by the owner's mechanical integrity program, which draws on API 570 for piping and API 510 for pressure vessels, with welding procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX and new piping built to ASME B31.3. For a candidate headed for refinery work, the ASME Part C option, Section IX (2023 edition) with B31.1 and B31.3 (2024 editions), matches the paperwork on the job. Further reading: ASME Section IX and ASME B31.3.

Turnaround inspection is as much paperwork as weld watching. Weld maps, welder logs, preheat and post-weld heat treatment charts, material verification records and pressure test packages all have to line up before a unit can restart, and the inspector who keeps them current saves the job a great deal of grief at the end.

Data center campuses in Caddo and Bossier parishes

In an August 2026 update Amazon described two data center campuses across Caddo and Bossier parishes and a third planned in Shreveport, and said the developer and owner, STACK Infrastructure, expects up to 2,250 construction jobs. Amazon also said it plans workforce programs with local educational institutions and technical colleges. Data center construction is heavy on structural steel, equipment platforms, pipe supports and mechanical piping for cooling systems, built to the project specifications.

On that kind of job a welding inspector checks shop drawings against what arrives, confirms welder qualifications for field welds, inspects moment connections, embeds, stairs and supports, and documents repairs. Structural steel is generally welded to AWS D1.1, which is the Part C book most building construction inspectors choose. Mechanical contractors installing chilled water and other piping systems may point their inspectors toward the ASME package instead. Background: AWS D1.1.

Building at Barksdale Air Force Base

Military construction continues at Barksdale. In July 2026 NAVFAC Southeast announced a contract to BL Harbert International for a four-story dormitory that will house 192 personnel supporting the base's new Weapons Generation Facility, with completion set for February 2029. The notice describes a pile-supported reinforced concrete foundation, insulated masonry walls and a standing seam metal roof, so this particular building is not a steel-frame job. Even so, a building like that still carries welded steel lintels, embedded plates, stairs, rails, roof framing and mechanical piping, and the federal construction specifications for the project name the welding code and the inspection and records expected. A CWI working for a contractor on base has to work from those specifications line by line rather than from habits picked up on commercial jobs.

Pipe from the Port of Caddo-Bossier

Benteler Steel/Tube runs a hot-rolled seamless tube mill at the Port of Caddo-Bossier that makes drill pipe, tubing, line pipe, structural pipe, coupling stock and casing, and in April 2024 it announced a new threading facility for seamless tubes to extend its oil country tubular goods work. Seamless pipe has no longitudinal weld, so most inspection inside the mill is product testing rather than welding inspection. The welding questions come later, when that line pipe and structural pipe is joined in the field or in fabrication shops, and when the mill's own maintenance crews repair equipment. For a Shreveport inspector the mill matters mostly as a source of material: knowing how seamless pipe is made, marked and certified helps when reviewing material records on a job.

Welding training in northwest Louisiana

Northwest Louisiana Technical Community College has campuses in Shreveport, Minden and Mansfield and celebrated its 90th anniversary at the Shreveport campus in August 2026. Federal completion data for the 2025 award year, as summarized by tradecolleges.org, show 79 welding certificate graduates at the college. A technical college welding certificate usually places a CWI applicant on the trade or vocational line of the AWS experience table, though AWS reviews each program and makes the decision. Before you apply, ask the college for a transcript that shows the welding courses and hours, because AWS reads the evidence, not the program name.

Finding an AWS section from Shreveport

We could not confirm an AWS section that meets in Shreveport itself. AWS District 9 lists Louisiana sections that include Central Louisiana, Baton Rouge and New Orleans. The section finder on aws.org shows which section serves your ZIP code and when its next technical meeting is. Section meetings are worth the drive: they are where you meet practising CWIs who can tell you how local employers use the credential, and after certification, technical programs can contribute professional development hours toward recertification.

Getting to a Part B site from Shreveport

Parts A and C are computer-based tests taken at a Prometric test center after AWS approves your application. Part B is not. AWS runs the practical at its seminar locations, usually on the weekend after a three-day Part B seminar held Wednesday through Friday at the same site. The AWS list of CWI training locations has no site in north Louisiana; Dallas, Beaumont and Houston in Texas, Tulsa in Oklahoma and New Orleans are the listed sites a Shreveport candidate will most likely compare. For US exams with a Part B, AWS requires the application six weeks before the Part B date, and every part needs at least 72 percent to pass.

Part B asks 46 questions about hands-on work with the specimens, tools and documents AWS issues, including applying a procedure specification and its qualification record. Practise with fillet, bridge cam and undercut gauges on real welds until the readings are quick and dependable, and budget the trip with the CWI exam cost calculator.

Pipeline years, turnaround years: proving your experience

AWS balances schooling against welding-related work. Its CWI page sets one year for a bachelor's degree or higher in welding engineering or technology, two for an associate degree or higher in welding or a related engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, three for engineering or technical courses applicable to a welding bachelor's degree, four for completed trade or vocational courses, five for a high school diploma or equivalent, nine for eighth-grade schooling and twelve for less.

The hard part for many Shreveport candidates is not the number of years but the paper trail. Pipeline spreads and turnarounds are short contracts with different companies, and a welder can work for six contractors in three years. Keep a running log of each job: the contractor, the dates, the owner, the processes and pipe or plate you welded, the code or specification, and the name and contact details of a supervisor or inspector who will confirm it. Welder qualification test records and badge cards help show the welding side of the work. You also need a passing AWS vision test, recorded on the AWS visual acuity form and timed so it is current when you sit the exam. The CWI requirements guide explains how AWS reads an application.

Six days between spreads

Field work in the Haynesville comes in long rotations with short breaks, which is why the online format has no scheduled class times. You set the pace, work through the material when you are home, and send questions to the instructor, who replies in writing. A practical order is fundamentals and welding symbols before the application goes in, the code book while AWS reviews it, and the timed practice papers in the final stretch before Part A. Candidates who want the six days done in one break often book the one-to-one format, online or in person, and spend the time on whichever part worries them most.

A crew course at a Shreveport yard or site

A pipeline contractor, fabrication shop or mechanical contractor with several candidates can have the six days delivered at its yard or project office. The group uses its own weld samples and gauges, and the code sessions follow the book most of the crew will choose: API 1104 for a pipeline company, D1.1 for a steel erector, the ASME package for a piping contractor. Contractors often schedule the course before bidding work that names a CWI in the specification. Even in a crew course, each welder or inspector applies to AWS alone and supplies a personal vision record and experience evidence.

After the CWI: endorsements, API certification and NDT

AWS certification lasts nine years, with renewal applications at years three and six; at nine years AWS offers recertification by retaking Part B, by 80 professional development hours, through the Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential, through an endorsement exam passed before year nine, through the Senior CWI exams or through the nine-year course. Inspectors who stay in refining often go on to an API individual certification such as API 570 for piping or API 510 for pressure vessels; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers those examinations and certifies the inspectors.

NDT methods are the other common next step, certified by the employer under its written practice. Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including UT Level 2 for pipe and vessel thickness and weld work, MT Level 2, PT Level 2 and VT Level 2. Local pages: NDT training in Shreveport, ultrasonic testing in Shreveport, magnetic particle testing in Shreveport and Practical NDT simulator access from Shreveport. CWI exam prep in nearby cities: Dallas, Lake Charles, Baton Rouge and Tulsa.

Sending a Shreveport enquiry

Tell us the format you want, how many people need preparing, the Part C book each plans to take and roughly when they hope to sit the exam. For a crew course, list the rotations or project milestones to work around. If an experience record is scattered across many short contracts, describe it and we will suggest what to confirm with AWS before applying. Each format is quoted on request, and we answer every enquiry within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Shreveport?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Shreveport. The six days are taken online at your own pace, at your employer's yard or site as a group, or one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits Haynesville pipeline work?
faq.a: API 1104, 22nd edition, the standard most US pipeline girth welds are qualified and accepted against. If you mainly inspect compressor or treating station piping, compare it with the ASME package.

faq.q: Which code should a refinery inspector in Shreveport choose?
faq.a: Usually the ASME package: Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3. Refinery welding procedures and welders are qualified to Section IX, and new process piping is built to B31.3.

faq.q: Where would a Shreveport candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location. The AWS list has no north Louisiana site; Dallas, Beaumont, Houston, Tulsa and New Orleans are the listed sites most likely to suit.

faq.q: I have worked for many pipeline and turnaround contractors. How do I document experience?
faq.a: Keep a log for each contract with dates, owner, processes, materials, the code you worked to and a supervisor who can confirm it. Welder qualification records help. AWS decides what counts.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Shreveport?
faq.a: We could not confirm one that meets in Shreveport. AWS District 9 lists Louisiana sections including Central Louisiana, Baton Rouge and New Orleans, and the section finder on aws.org shows the section for your ZIP code.

faq.q: Can a pipeline or mechanical contractor host the six days?
faq.a: Yes. In the corporate format the six days are delivered at the contractor's yard or project office, using its own samples and gauges. Each person still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Does the course lead on to API 570 or API 510?
faq.a: Many refinery CWIs later sit an API individual certification. Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation separately; API administers those examinations and certifies inspectors.
No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no window into AWS examination content or results. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I get a quote from Shreveport?
faq.a: Write to us through the enquiry link on this page with the format, the number of people and their Part C books. We quote every format on request and reply within one business day.
